title: PaO₂ / FiO₂ (P/F) Ratio
sources: ARDS Definition Task Force. Berlin definition, JAMA 2012
purpose: Grades the severity of hypoxaemic respiratory failure and, with PEEP ≥ 5 cmH₂O and the other Berlin criteria, classifies ARDS. Trended for ventilator and adjunct-therapy decisions (proning, neuromuscular blockade, ECMO referral).

interpretation.label: ≤ 100 — SEVERE ARDS (with PEEP ≥ 5). Prone positioning + neuromuscular blockade; refer for ECMO if refractory (PaO₂/FiO₂ < 80 despite optimisation, EOLIA-style criteria)
100–200 — MODERATE ARDS (with PEEP ≥ 5). Consider proning; strict lung-protective ventilation
> 300 — does not meet the ARDS oxygenation threshold

notes: Berlin ARDS also requires: onset within 1 week of a known insult, bilateral opacities not fully explained by effusion / collapse / nodules, and respiratory failure not fully explained by cardiac failure / fluid overload (objective assessment, e.g. echo, if no risk factor). The P/F falls at altitude — a correction (P/F × barometric pressure / 760) exists. When there's no ABG, S/F ratio ≈ 315 → P/F 300 and S/F ≈ 235 → P/F 200 (SpO₂ ≤ 97%).
buildNote: Formula engine. An S/F-ratio variant and a PEEP-gate reminder are refinements.
